statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6637 (refint allows stack buffer overflow and SQL injection) in 16.14 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6637/ lists 16.14 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.14 are affected; the component is the contrib module refint), and the 16.14 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.14/, list it under 'Prevent SQL injection and buffer overruns in contrib/spi'. The fix is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/710995782fa388f3878a86e1d9ed68db8abc4276 (refint: Fix SQL injection and buffer overruns, tagged Security: CVE-2026-6637), which changes only contrib/spi/refint.c and is in the REL_16_14 release tag and not in REL_16_13. It replaces the fixed 8192-byte query buffers in check_primary_key() and check_foreign_key() with growable strings, and quotes cascaded key values with quote_literal_cstr() instead of wrapping some types in bare single quotes. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; its 16.14-r0 security upgrade, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/commit/56de254843f841a99aedea4953a2dc9ec9338eb4, lists CVE-2026-6637 under the 16.14-r0 secfixes. We checked every postgresql16 and postgresql16-contrib build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index. The refint module ships as /usr/lib/postgresql16/refint.so in the postgresql16-contrib package. In 16.13-r0 on both architectures refint.so still holds the old format string ' %s = %s%s%s %s ' and imports SPI_gettype, and does not import quote_literal_cstr; in 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 on both architectures the old format string and the SPI_gettype import are gone, and refint.so imports quote_literal_cstr and holds the new format string ' %s = %s ' that the fix adds (check_foreign_key is present in every build as a positive control). The postgres server binaries report PostgreSQL 16.13, 16.14, 16.15 and 16.16 respectively. 16.14-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix, and 16.13-r0 is affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6637 (PostgreSQL refint allows stack buffer overflow and SQL injection) in 17.10 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6637/ lists 17.10 as the fixed release for major version 17 (versions before 17.10 are affected), and the 17.10 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.10/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/2dc64ef28b3696d202628f852c6a97ae8a2e2a62 on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes only contrib/spi/refint.c: check_primary_key() and check_foreign_key() build their SQL in a growable StringInfo instead of fixed 8192-byte stack buffers, and check_foreign_key() quotes new key values with quote_literal_cstr(); it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-6637 and is in the REL_17_10 release tag and not in REL_17_9. The refint module ships in the postgresql17-contrib package as /usr/lib/postgresql17/refint.so. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 17.10-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/2949d6752d74a3fb36bd772b9f993331fa6917e2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, differs from the 17.9-r0 one only in the version, the tarball checksum and the secfixes list, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6637 under its 17.10-r0 secfixes. We checked refint.so, with the server binary's version string for each build, in every postgresql17 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index: 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 and 17.9-r0 report PostgreSQL 17.7, 17.8 and 17.9 and are affected, while 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 report 17.10, 17.11 and 17.12 and carry the fix. As a check, refint.so imports quote_literal_cstr in 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 on both architectures and not in 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 or 17.9-r0, and the old cascade-update format string the fix removes (' %s = %s%s%s %s ') is present in 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 and 17.9-r0 and absent from the later builds. 17.10-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
